newsitem.title: USA: Vandalism probed against Miami Jewish, black graves.
newsitem.headline: Vandalism probed against Miami Jewish, black graves.

text.p: A historic cemetery where some of Miami's first citizens are buried was hit by vandals intent on destroying the graves of blacks and Jews, police said Thursday.
Some tombstones -- many of them inscribed with Hebrew letters -- were smashed to pieces.

"Whoever did this was not just out for a night of drunken fun, they were obviously, consciously trying to wreak havoc at the cemetery," said Bill Schwartz, spokesman for the Miami Police Department, noting that 57 graves had been vandalised overnight Saturday.
"No matter how you cut it, it's a hate crime, not only because the large number of damaged tombs were of Jewish people and of black people," he said.
The 99-year-old cemetery, one year younger than the city of Miami, was originally segregated, so Jewish and black graves were in separate sections.
